verses.note: Paul reads the verse as God counting a person righteous apart from works, since Abram was declared righteous before circumcision and before the law (Romans 4:3-11, Galatians 3:6). James cites it to show that such faith is proved in obedience (James 2:21-23). Protestants have usually read ‘credited’ as God reckoning a righteousness not one's own; Roman Catholic and Orthodox readers have stressed that God's reckoning also makes a person righteous. All agree that the verse puts God's promise and Abram's trust before any merit.
